chunks.arabic_text: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، الصَّنْعَانِيُّ، الْيَمَانِيُّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا إِسْحَاقَ.

translations.en: Ibrahim ibn Umar, al-San'ani, al-Yamani, known by the kunya Abu Ishaq.

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَر، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ). وَلَهُ كِتَابٌ.

translations.en: Very weak. He narrated from Abu Ja'far, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them). He has a book.

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī's *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Ṣanʿānī as 'very weak' (ḍaʿīf jiddan), a critical designation in Shia hadith sciences indicating significant flaws in memory or precision despite his transmission from the Sixth and Seventh Imams. His authorship of a standalone book suggests he was a prolific, albeit less reliable, transmitter whose works require careful scrutiny by scholars of rijal. This assessment highlights the rigorous standards applied to Yemeni narrators within the broader corpus of Shia biographical evaluation.
en.seo_question: Who is Ibrahim ibn al-San'ani and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا: Very weak (a technical term in hadith criticism indicating low reliability)
key_terms.يُكْنَى: Known by the kunya (a teknonym or honorific name)
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Abu Ja'far (referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: Book (referring to a written work or collection by the narrator)
